name: Deep ITM Long Call (stock replacement)
summary: Buy a 0.80-0.90 delta call as a capital-efficient substitute for 100 shares, paying a small time premium for a built-in floor.
max_profit: Unlimited: tracks the stock nearly 1:1 above the strike, minus the extrinsic paid
max_loss: Debit paid x 100 - far less than the cost of 100 shares, but still a total loss if the stock falls below the strike and stays there.

greeks.theta: small negative - only the thin extrinsic decays; typically < 0.3%/day of the debit
greeks.vega: small positive (deep ITM has little vega)

when_to_use: When you want long exposure but do not want to tie up $X0,000 in shares, and the extrinsic (time value) in the deep ITM call is under ~2% of the strike. Best when IVR < 40 and the name has tight deep-ITM markets.
entry_rules: Extrinsic value = call mid - max(0, spot - strike); require extrinsic <= 2% of strike price
60-180 DTE so the thin extrinsic decays slowly
Bid/ask <= 3% of mid - deep ITM markets are often wide; reject the trade if they are
Debit <= 6% of equity (~$3,000 on $50k) per position
Skip any name where a dividend is large enough that the call's extrinsic is less than the dividend at entry (you forfeit dividends as a call holder)
management_rules: Manage the position like a stock position: hold while the daily trend is intact (price above the 50 EMA)
Roll out when DTE falls below 45: sell the current call, buy the same-delta call 90+ days out, in one net order
Stop at -35% of the debit or a daily close below the 50 EMA, whichever first
Take partial profits at +50% of the debit; let the balance run with a trailing stop 1.5 ATR below price
exit_rules: Sell to close on the stop, the trend break, or at 45 DTE (roll or exit)

NEVER hold into expiration week: an ITM call at expiry is auto-exercised and buys 100 shares at the strike, which on a $500 underlying is a $50,000 debit the account cannot fund. Hard flatten/roll by 5 trading days before expiry
assignment_risk: No assignment (long). Exercise risk is the danger: auto-exercise creates a large unfunded share purchase. Also note you receive no dividends and have no voting rights versus owning the stock.
buying_power: Debit only. This is the entire point - roughly 10-20% of the cash needed for 100 shares.
liquidity_needs: Needs a real deep-ITM market. Reject if bid/ask > 3% of mid or OI < 100 on that strike.
common_mistakes: Paying too much extrinsic and turning a stock proxy into a decaying bet; forgetting there is no dividend and being out-returned by the shareholder; letting it go to expiry and triggering a six-figure exercise.
